notes: Credit the sunken ship's name to Bulgarian media, not to Bulgaria's Prime Minister: in the standfirst, lede, Black Sea section and key points say Bulgarian media identified the sunken general cargo ship as the Azov Concord, that a maritime source said the vessel was in the search and rescue rather than hit, and that the President's office named the hull HS Dignity, Guinea-Bissau flagged, so its identity and flag are not settled.

Keep the eight Azerbaijani crew Azerbaijan confirmed rescued with the Chelsea 3, not the Azov Concord: Bulgaria's Interior Ministry said the sunken ship's crew were mainly Syrians with three Egyptians, while the Chelsea 3's 15 crew were seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis.

In the Black Sea section and the key points, report the second ship as the Maltese-flagged, Ukrainian-owned general cargo ship Chelsea 3, hit by three drones 18 nautical miles east of Byala with all 15 crew rescued and five injured and left drifting without her crew: credit Bulgaria's Prime Minister and Vanguard Tech, per Seatrade, and drop the Russian channel's Chelsea-7 and any line saying she sank.

In the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf section, name the 7 October tanker as the Acers: the IMO's confirmed incidents list gives that hull the name Acers (IMO 9301902). Report that UKMTO logged a tanker hit by multiple projectiles about 51 nautical miles off Qatar on 7 October, with casualties reported, and give the ship as the Acers. Then add what is new in one sentence: the Philippines' Department of Migrant Workers said the injured seafarer is being treated in Doha and the other 24 Filipino crew are safe. That paragraph must carry the name, not only the Sources heading.

In the headline, standfirst and lede keep the sinking and the missing crew with the identification of the lead story: say Bulgarian media identified the sunken general cargo ship Azov Concord, hit by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast on 13 October, with 11 crew missing. Credit the identification to Bulgarian media once, not twice, and do not let the 11 crew missing fall out of the headline and lede into the key points only.
